<margin>A 16</margin> I commend to you our sister Phoebe, who is in the service <note>original: "ministerio"</note> of the church which is at Cenchreae <note>The eastern port of Corinth.</note>: so that you may receive her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her in whatever business she may have need of you. For she herself has also assisted many, and myself as well. Greet Prisca and Aquila, my helpers in CHRIST JESUS (who risked their own necks for my life; to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles) and the church in their house. Greet Epenetus, my beloved, who is the first-fruit <note>original: "primitiuus"</note> of the church of Asia in CHRIST JESUS. Greet Mary, who has labored much among you. Greet Andronicus and Julia <note>Many manuscripts read "Junia" here.</note>, my kinsmen and fellow prisoners, who are noble among the apostles, and who were in CHRIST before me.

<margin>B</margin> Greet Ampliatus, most dear to me in the Lord. Greet Urbanus, our helper in CHRIST JESUS, and my beloved Stachys. Greet Apelles, approved in CHRIST. Greet those who are of the household of Aristobulus. Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet those of the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord. Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Greet the most dear Persis, who has labored much in the Lord. Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine. Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers who are with them. Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympias, and all the saints who are with them.

### Epistle to the Corinthians

<margin>B</margin> ...appoint those who are least esteemed in the church to judge. I say this to your shame. Is it so that there is not even one wise man among you who could judge between his brothers? Instead, brother contends in judgment with brother—and this before unbelievers? Now, therefore, it is altogether a fault among you that you have lawsuits with one another. Why do you not rather accept injury? Why do you not rather suffer fraud? But you yourselves do wrong and defraud, and even your own brothers. Or do you not know that the wicked will not possess the kingdom of God? Do not be led astray: neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor the effeminate, nor those who lie with men, nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor slanderers, nor the rapacious, will possess the kingdom of God.

<margin>C</margin> And such were some of you; but you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of our Lord **JESUS CHRIST** and in the spirit of our God. All things are lawful for me, but not all things are helpful. All things are lawful for me, but I will not be brought under the power of any. Food for the belly and the belly for food; but God will destroy both it and them. Now the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body. Truly, God both raised up the Lord and will raise us up by His power. Do you not know that your bodies are members of **CHRIST**? Shall I then, taking the members of **CHRIST**, make them members of a prostitute?

<margin>D</margin> Heaven forbid! Or do you not know that he who is joined to a prostitute is made one body? For "they shall be," he says, "two in one flesh" <note>A quotation from Genesis 2:24, establishing the theological basis for sexual union</note>. But he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit. Flee from fornication. Every sin that a man commits is outside the body; but he who commits fornication sins against his own body. Or do you not know that your members are a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God, and you are not your own? For you were bought at a great price. Glorify and carry God in your body.

<margin>A VII</margin> **D** Now concerning the things about which you wrote to me: It is good for a man not to touch a woman; but because of fornication, let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband.

Why do you not rather endure injury? Why do you not rather tolerate the loss of things? But you yourselves inflict injury and take away spoils—and this from brothers. Do you not know that the unjust will not inherit the kingdom of God? <margin>33</margin> Do not be led astray: neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor the effeminate, nor the unchaste <note>original: "cinædi"; a specific term for those engaging in passive homosexual acts</note>, nor the greedy, nor thieves, nor drunkards, nor the abusive, nor the rapacious will inherit the kingdom of God. <margin>34</margin> ¶ And such you were once; but you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of our Lord **JESUS CHRIST** and in the spirit of our God. <margin>35</margin> ¶ All things are in my power, but not all things are profitable. ### II Corinthians 16

Let the husband render the due benevolence <note>original: *beniuolentiam*; a traditional term for the "marital debt" or physical affection owed within marriage</note> to the wife. Likewise also the wife to the husband. The wife does not have power over her own body, but the husband. In the same manner also the husband does not have power over his own body, but <margin>40</margin> the wife. ¶ Do not deprive one another: unless perhaps by consent for a time, so that you may devote yourselves to fasting and prayer. And come together again, lest Satan tempt you because of your lack of self-control <note>original: *incontinentiam*</note>. However, I say this by permission, not <margin>41</margin> by command. ¶ For I would that all men were even as myself. But everyone has his own gift from God: one in this way, another in that. <margin>42</margin> ¶ I say to those who are without a wife and to those who are widows: it is good for them if they remain even as I. But if they cannot contain themselves, let them marry. For it is better to marry than to experience the fire <note>an idiom for being consumed by desire or passion</note>. <margin>43</margin> ¶ But to those who are joined in marriage, it is not I who command, but the Lord: let the wife not be separated from the husband. ¶ But if she is separated, let her remain unmarried, or be reconciled to her husband. And let the husband <margin>44</margin> not put away his wife. ¶ To the rest, however, I say, not the Lord: if any brother has an unbelieving wife and she consents to live with him, let him not put her away. And if any wife has an unbelieving husband and he consents to live with her, let her not put him away. For the unbelieving husband is sanctified in the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified in the husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean; but now <margin>45</margin> they are holy. ¶ But if the unbeliever departs, let him depart. For a brother or sister is not subject to servitude <note>original: *seruituti*; implying that the marriage bond does not enslave a believer if an unbelieving spouse leaves</note> in such cases. For God has called us in peace. For how do you know, wife, if you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, if you will save your wife? Nothing, except as <margin>46</margin> God has distributed to each. ¶ As God has called each one, so let him walk. And so I ordain in all the churches. Was anyone called being circumcised? Let him not become uncircumcised. Was anyone called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised. Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but the keeping of the commandments of God. <margin>47</margin> ¶ Let each one remain in the calling in which he was called. Were you called as a servant <note>original: *seruus*; usually referring to a slave in the Roman context</note>? Let it not be a care to you. Nevertheless, if you are able to become free, make the greater effort <note>original: *maiorem opam impende*</note>.

<column-break/>

Let the husband render the debt to the wife; and likewise also the wife to the husband. The woman does not have power over her own body, but the husband. Likewise also the husband does not have power over his own body, but the woman. Do not defraud <note>original: *fraudare*; a more legalistic term for withholding what is due</note> one another, unless perhaps by consent for a time, that you may devote yourselves to prayer. And return again to the same, lest Satan tempt you because of your lack of self-control. This, however, I say by way of indulgence <note>original: *indulgentiam*; suggesting a concession to human weakness</note>, not <margin>B</margin> by way of command. For I want all of you to be as I am myself. But everyone has his own gift from God: one indeed thus, another truly thus. I say to the unmarried and to the widows: it is good for them if they remain so, even as I. But if they do not contain themselves, let them marry. For it is better to marry than to burn. To those who are joined in marriage, I command—not I, but the Lord—that the wife should not depart from the husband. But if she departs, she must remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband. And the husband should not put away his wife.

<margin>C</margin>
For to the rest I say, not the Lord: If any brother has an unbelieving wife and she consents to live with him, let him not put her away. And if any woman has an unbelieving husband and he consents to live with her, let she not put away the husband. For the unbelieving husband is sanctified through the faithful wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified through the faithful husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean; but now they are holy. But if the unbeliever departs, let him depart. For a brother or sister is not subject to servitude in such a case. For God has called you in peace. For how do you know, woman, if you will save your husband? Or how do you know, man, if you will make your woman safe? Unless to each as the Lord has divided. <margin>D</margin> As God has called each one, so let him walk, and as I teach in all the churches. Was anyone called being circumcised? Let him not bring on a foreskin. Was anyone called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised. Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but the keeping of the commandments of God. Let each one remain in whatever calling he was called. Were you called as a servant? Let it not be a care to you. But even if you can become free, use it rather.

### A VII

<margin>B</margin>
...in the church, appoint them to judge. I say this to your shame. Is there not one wise person among you who can judge between his brothers? Do you not know: that the unjust will not possess the kingdom of God? All things are lawful for me: but not all things are expedient. All things are lawful for me: but I will not be brought under the power of any. for he who is called in the Lord as a servant <note>original: *seruus*; while often translated as servant, in the Roman context this specifically refers to an enslaved person</note>: is the Lord’s freedman. But if you take a wife: you have not sinned. And if a virgin marries: she has not sinned. Nevertheless, such as these shall have tribulation of the flesh. But I spare you. And so I say this, brothers. The time is short. It remains: that both those who have wives / should be as though not having them. & those who weep: as though not weeping. & those who rejoice: as though not rejoicing. & those who buy: as though not possessing. & those who use this world: as though they use it not. <margin>F</margin> For the form of this world is passing away. that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up: but charity <note>original: *charitas*; the Latin term for "caritas" or selfless, Christian love</note> indeed builds up. If anyone thinks he knows something: he has not yet known it in the way he ought to know it. If anyone

### THE EPISTLE

...am. For you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord. My defense to those who examine me is this: Do we not have the right to eat and drink? Do we not have the right to take along a sister as a companion <note>original: *mulierem sororem*; literally "a woman sister," referring to a Christian woman or wife</note>, as do the other apostles, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas <note>The Aramaic name for the Apostle Peter</note>? Or is it only Barnabas and I who do not have the right to refrain from manual labor? Who ever serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat of its fruit? Who tends a flock and 
<margin>B</margin>
does not drink the milk from the flock? Do I say these things merely from a human perspective? Does the Law not also say this? For it is written in the Law of Moses: "You shall not muzzle the mouth of an ox while it treads out the grain." <note>Deuteronomy 25:4</note> Is God concerned with oxen? Or does He say this entirely for our sake? Indeed, it was written for our sake, because the plowman ought to plow in hope, and the thresher in hope of receiving the fruit. If we have sown spiritual things for you, is it a great thing if we reap your material goods? If others share in this right over you, do we not have it even more? But we have not used this right; instead, we endure all things so that we may not place any obstacle in the way of the Gospel of CHRIST. <summary>In this passage from 1 Corinthians 9, the Apostle Paul defends his apostolic authority and explains why he chooses to forgo his right to financial support from the church. He argues that just as soldiers, farmers, and priests are supported by their work, he has a right to material support, but waives it to avoid hindering the Gospel.</summary>

## THE SECOND EPISTLE TO THE CORINTHIANS, PAGE 18

...under the law <note>The Mosaic Law of the Old Testament</note> I became as if I were under the law (though I myself was not under the law) so that I might win those who were under the law. To those who were without the law, I became as if I were without the law (though I was not without the law of God, but was under the law of CHRIST) so that I might win those who were without the law. To the weak I became weak, so that I might win the weak. I have become all things to all people, so that I might save all. I do all things for the sake of the gospel, so that I may be made a sharer in it. Do you not know that those who run in a stadium all indeed run, but only one receives the prize <note>original: *brauium*; from the Greek *brabeion*, the award given to the winner of a race</note>? So run, that you may obtain it. Every man who competes in a contest <note>original: *agone*; refers to the intense physical struggle of ancient Greek athletics</note> abstains from all things. They do it to receive a perishable crown, but we an imperishable one. I therefore run in this way, not as if toward an uncertain goal; I fight in this way, not as if beating the air; but I discipline my body and bring it into subjection, lest perhaps, after I have preached to others, I myself should be disqualified <note>original: *reprobus*; meaning "rejected" or "failing the test"</note>.

For I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers: that our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea, and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea, and all ate the same spiritual food <note>A reference to Manna, the "bread from heaven" provided to the Israelites in the wilderness</note>, and all drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them; and that rock was CHRIST.

Now these things were done as examples for us <note>original: *in figura*; literally "in a figure" or "as a type," a common way of reading the Old Testament as a foreshadowing of the New</note>, so that we should not be desirers of evil things, as they also desired. # EPISTLE TO THE CORINTHIANS

...became seekers of evil things. Therefore, let him who thinks he stands take heed lest he fall. No temptation has overtaken you except what is common to man. But God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able; but with the temptation, he will also provide a way out <note>original: *proventum*; literally an "issue" or "outcome"</note>, so that you may be able to endure it. For this reason, my most <margin>D</margin> beloved: flee from the worship of idols. I speak as to wise men: judge for yourselves what I say. The cup of blessing which we bless: is it not the participation <note>original: *communicatio*; sharing in or communion with</note> in the blood of CHRIST? And the bread which we break: is it not the participation in the body of the Lord? Since there is one bread, we who are many are one body: all we who participate in the one bread and the one cup. Consider Israel <margin>E</margin> according to the flesh. Are not those who eat the sacrifices participants in the altar? What then? Do I say that what is sacrificed to idols is anything, or that an idol itself is anything? No, but the things the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God. I do not want you to become associates of demons. You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You cannot be participants in the table of the Lord and the table of demons. Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he? All things are lawful for me, but not all things are helpful. All things are lawful for me, but not all things build up. Let no one seek what is his own, <margin>F</margin> but what belongs to another. Everything that is sold in the meat market <note>original: *macello*; the ancient Roman provisions market where meat from public sacrifices was often sold</note>: eat it, asking no questions for the sake of conscience. The earth is the Lord's, and its fullness. If any of the unbelievers invites you to a meal and you wish to go: eat whatever is set before you, asking no questions for the sake of <margin>G</margin> conscience. But if anyone should say, "This was sacrificed to idols": do not eat it for the sake of the one who pointed it out and for the sake of conscience. Now, I say conscience—not yours, but the other person's. For why is my liberty judged by another's conscience? If I participate with grace <note>original: *gratia*; can mean "with thankfulness" or "by God's grace"</note>: why am I slandered for that for which I give thanks? Therefore, whether you eat or drink, or whatever else you do: do all for the glory of God. Be without offense to the Jews and the Gentiles and to the church of God: just as I also please everyone in all things, not seeking what is for my own...

The bread which we break: is it not the communion of the body of CHRIST? Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body. For we all participate in one bread. That an idol is anything, or that what is sacrificed to an idol is anything? No. But truly, those things which the Gentiles sacrifice: they sacrifice to demons and not to God. Are we stronger than he? ¶ All things are in <margin>70</margin> my power: but not all things are profitable. All things are in my power: but not all things build up. Everything that is sold in the meat market: eat, inquiring nothing for the sake of conscience; for the earth is the Lord's and the fullness thereof. ¶ If any <margin>71</margin> of the unbelievers summons you and you wish to go: eat everything that is set before you, inquiring nothing for the sake of conscience. But if anyone says to you, "This is sacrificed to idols": do not eat for the sake of the one who pointed it out and for the sake of conscience (for the earth is the Lord's and the fullness thereof). But I say conscience: not your own, but the other's. For why is my liberty judged by another's conscience? If I participate with grace: why am I slandered for that for which I give thanks? Be without offense to the Jews and the Gentiles and the church of God: just as I also please all in all things, not seeking my own...

<margin>72</margin> [...not seeking my own] utility, but that of the many, so that they may be saved. <note>This completes the thought from the previous page: "not seeking my own advantage, but that of many."</note>
<margin>1</margin> Be imitators of me, even as I also am of CHRIST. I praise you, brothers, that you are mindful of all my affairs, and just as I delivered them to you, you hold fast to my traditions.
<margin>73</margin> ¶ But I would have you know that the head of every man is CHRIST; the head of the woman is the man; and the head of CHRIST is God. Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered brings shame upon his head. Every woman also, praying or prophesying with her head not covered, brings shame upon her head. For it is one and the same thing as if she were shaven. Therefore, if a woman is not veiled, let her be shorn. But if it is disgraceful for a woman to be shorn or shaved, let her be veiled. For a man ought not to veil his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of the man. 
<margin>74</margin> ¶ For man is not from woman, but woman from man. Neither indeed was man created for the sake of the woman, but woman for the sake of the man. 
<margin>75</margin> For this reason the woman ought to have authority <note>original: *potestatem*; traditionally interpreted here as a sign of authority, such as a veil</note> on her head, because of the angels. ¶ Nevertheless, neither is the man without the woman, nor the woman without the man, in the Lord. For as the woman is from the man, so also is the man through the woman. But all things 
<margin>76</margin> are from God. ¶ Judge for yourselves: is it proper for a woman to pray to God unveiled? Does not nature itself teach you that if a man grows his hair long, it is a disgrace to him? But if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her, because her hair is 
<margin>77</margin> given to her for a covering. ¶ But if anyone seems to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor do the churches of 
<margin>78</margin> God. ¶ In giving this warning, I do not praise you, for you come together not for the better, but for the worse. First of all, when you come together in the church, I hear that there are schisms <note>original: *schismata*; divisions or factions</note> among you, and I partly believe it. For there must also be heresies <note>original: *haereses*; here meaning sectarian groups or choices that divide the community</note> among you, so that those who are proven may be made manifest among 
<margin>79</margin> you. ¶ Therefore, when you come together in one place, it is no longer to eat the Lord’s Supper. For each one takes his own supper beforehand while eating; and one is hungry, while another is drunk. Do you not have houses for eating and drinking? But if anyone seems to be contentious: we have no such custom, nor do the churches of God. But I command this, 
<margin>D</margin> not praising you, that you come together not for the better but for the worse. But now there are indeed many members, but one <margin>90</margin> body. ¶ And the eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no use for you," or again the head to the feet, "I do not need you." But our beautiful parts have no need. But God has tempered the body, giving more ample honor to that which suffered lack, so that there should be no discord in the body, but that the members should care for one another. # 1 CORINTHIANS XII–XIV

->EPI.<-

...do they all have the grace of healings? Do all speak with tongues? Do all interpret? But strive for the better gifts. And I show you a still more excellent way.
<margin>A XIII</margin>
If I speak with the tongues of men and angels, but have not charity <note>original: *charitatem*. This traditional term implies a sacrificial, divine love.</note>, I have become like sounding brass or a tinkling cymbal. And if I should have prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I should have all faith so that I could move mountains, but have not charity, I am nothing. <margin>B</margin> And if I should distribute all my goods to feed the poor, and if I should deliver my body so that I may burn, but have not charity, it profits me nothing. Charity is patient, it is kind. Charity does not envy, does not act perversely, is not puffed up; it is not ambitious. It does not seek its own; it is not provoked; it thinks no evil; it does not rejoice over iniquity, <margin>C</margin> but rejoices with the truth. It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Charity never fails: whether prophecies shall be emptied out, or tongues shall cease, or knowledge shall be destroyed. For we know in part, and we prophesy in part. But when that which is perfect has come, that which is in part shall be emptied out. When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I understood as a child, I thought <margin>D</margin> as a child. But when I became a man, I put away the things of a child. We see now through a mirror in an enigma <note>original: *in ænigmate*. A famous phrase often translated as "darkly," implying a blurred or indirect vision.</note>; but then face to face. Now I know in part; but then I shall know just as I am known. And now there remain faith, hope, and charity, these three: but the greatest of these is charity.
<margin>A XIIII</margin>
Follow after charity, strive for spiritual things: but more that you may prophesy. For he who speaks in a tongue speaks not to men, but to God; for no one hears. But in spirit he speaks mysteries. For he who prophesies speaks to men for edification, and exhortation, and consolation. He who speaks in a tongue edifies himself; but he who prophesies edifies the church of God. If I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love <note>original: *dilectionem*. Erasmus preferred this term over "charity" to emphasize a more personal affection or esteem.</note>, I have become resonating brass and a clanging cymbal. And if I have prophecy, and know all mysteries and all cognition, and if I have all faith so that I am able to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing. And if I deal out all my resources for food, and if I hand over my body so that I may burn, but have not love, I help nothing.

¶ Love is patient, it is kind, love does not envy, love does not act inconstantly, is not puffed up, does not work shamefully, does not seek its own, is not exasperated, does not impute evil, does not rejoice in injustice, but rejoices with the truth; it bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
<margin>93</margin>
Love never falls away. ¶ But whether prophecies shall be taken away, or tongues shall cease, or knowledge shall be <margin>94</margin> removed. ¶ For we know in part, and we prophesy in part. But when perfection has come, then that which is in part shall be removed. When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I felt as a child, I thought as a child. But truly when I became a man, I cast away those things which are a child's. For we see now through a mirror in a riddle; but then face to face. Now I know in part; then truly I shall know just as I also have been known. Now however there remain hope, faith, love—these three. But the greatest of these is love.
<margin>95</margin>
Pursue love. Strive for spiritual things, but truly that you may prophesy. For he who speaks in a tongue speaks not to men, but to God. For no one hears, but by the spirit he speaks mysteries. But he who prophesies speaks to men for edification, and exhortation, and <margin>96</margin> consolation. ¶ He who speaks in a tongue edifies himself; but he who prophesies edifies the church.

<summary>In this passage, Paul argues that prophecy is superior to speaking in tongues because it provides clear instruction and "edification" for the whole community. He uses analogies of musical instruments and the military trumpet to emphasize that spiritual gifts are only useful when they can be understood by others.</summary>

[Scri]ptures. And that he appeared to Cephas <note>original: "Cephe"—the Aramaic name for Peter the Apostle</note>: and after this to the eleven. Then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once / of whom many remain until now: but some have fallen asleep <note>fallen asleep: a common biblical metaphor for death</note>. Then he appeared to James. Then to all the apostles. But last of all
<margin>B</margin>
he appeared also to me, as if to one born out of time <note>original: "abortivo"—literally meaning a premature birth or a "miscarriage"; Paul uses this to highlight his unworthiness or his late arrival to the faith compared to the original apostles</note>. For I am the least of the apostles: who am not worthy to be called an apostle / because I persecuted the church of God. But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace in me was not empty / but I labored more abundantly than all of them. Yet not I: but the grace of God with me. For whether it was I / or they / so we preached: and so you believed. Now if CHRIST is preached, that he rose from the dead: how do some among you say / that there is no resurrection of the dead? But if there is no resurrection of the dead: then neither has CHRIST risen. And if CHRIST has not risen / our preaching is in vain / and your faith is also in vain. Moreover, we are found to be false witnesses
<margin>C</margin>
of God, because we have given testimony against God / that he raised CHRIST, whom he did not raise if the dead do not rise. For if the dead do not rise: neither has CHRIST risen. But if CHRIST has not risen: your faith is useless. For you are still in your sins. Therefore also those who have fallen asleep in CHRIST: have perished. If in this life only we are hoping in CHRIST: we are the most miserable of all men. But now CHRIST has risen from the dead, the firstfruits of those who sleep. For since by a man came death: also by a man came the resurrection of the dead. And just as in Adam all die: so also in CHRIST all shall be made alive. But each in his own order: the firstfruits, CHRIST. Then those who are of CHRIST: who believed in his coming. <header>EPISTLE</header>

<margin>C</margin>But I will remain at Ephesus until Pentecost <note>Pentecost: A Jewish harvest festival occurring fifty days after Passover, which early Christians also observed to commemorate the descent of the Holy Spirit</note>. For a great and evident door has been opened to me: and there are many adversaries. If Timothy comes: see that he is among you without fear. For he does the work of the Lord: just as I do. Therefore, let no one despise him. But send him on his way in peace: so that he may come to me. For I am waiting for him with the brothers. Concerning our brother Apollo: I make it known to you that
<margin>D</margin>I greatly urged him to come to you with the brothers. And it was certainly not his will to come now. But he will come: when he has time <note>original: "vacuū"—literally meaning leisure or an empty space in one's schedule</note>. Watch, stand firm in the faith, act like men <note>original: "viriliter agite"—an exhortation to courage or manliness</note>, and be strengthened: let all your things be done in love <note>original: "charitate"—the Greek term 'agape,' referring to selfless, Christian love</note>. Now I urge you, brothers—you know the household of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus, that they are the firstfruits of Achaia <note>Achaia: A Roman province in what is now southern Greece</note>, and they have dedicated themselves to the service of the saints: that you also be subject to such people / and to everyone who cooperates and labors. I rejoice at the presence of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus: because they have supplied what was lacking from you. For they have refreshed both my spirit
<margin>D</margin>and yours. Therefore, recognize those who are like this. All the churches of Asia greet you. Aquila and Priscilla greet you much in the Lord, along with the church in their house, with
<margin>A IVX</margin>whom I am also staying. All the brothers greet you. Greet one another: with a holy kiss. This greeting is in my own hand, Paul's. If anyone does not love our Lord JESUS CHRIST: let him be accursed <note>original: "anathema"—to be set apart for destruction or banned</note>. Our Lord comes <note>original: "maranatha"—an Aramaic phrase used by early Christians to express the longing for Christ's return</note>. The grace of our Lord JESUS CHRIST be with you. My love: be with you all in CHRIST JESUS. Amen.

But I will stay at Ephesus until Pentecost. For a great and effective door is opened to me: and there are many adversaries. ¶ If Timothy comes: see that he is secure among you. For he works the work of the Lord: as I also do. Therefore, let no one think nothing of him <note>original: "nichilipendat"—to belittle or value at nothing</note>: but leading him forward, send him on in peace / so that he may come to me. For I wait for him together with the brothers. ¶ Concerning our brother Apollo, I have exhorted him with many words / that he might go to you together with the brothers: but it was not at all his will / to go now. He will go, however: when it shall be opportune. ¶ Watch / stand in the faith / act like men / be strengthened: let all your things be done in love. ¶ Now I urge you brothers—you know the house of Stephanas, that they are the firstfruits of Achaia: and that they have dedicated themselves to serve the saints. I urge you, I say: that you also be subject to such ones / and to everyone cooperating and laboring. I rejoice moreover in the arrival of Stephanas / Fortunatus / and Achaicus. Because they have supplied my need. For they have revived <note>original: "refocillauerunt"—to warm again or refresh</note> my spirit and yours. Therefore, recognize them: for they are of this sort. ¶ The churches of Asia greet you. Aquila and Priscilla greet you very much in the Lord, with the church in their house. All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss. The greeting by my own hand, Paul's. If anyone does not love the Lord JESUS CHRIST, let him be accursed, our Lord comes. The grace of our Lord JESUS CHRIST be with you. My love be with all of you in CHRIST JESUS. Amen.

<margin>2</margin>
**STO.** ¶ Blessed be God, that is the father of our lord JESUS CHRIST, the father of mercies, and the God of all consolation: who consoles us in all our pressure <note>original: "pressura"—the Greek 'thlipsis' refers to being crushed or squeezed by circumstances; often translated as tribulation</note> noſtra. so that we also may be able to console those who are in any pressure: through the consolation by which we ourselves are consoled by God. Because as the sufferings of CHRIST abound in us: so through CHRIST our consolation also abounds. Whether however we are pressed for your consolation and salvation / or we are consoled for your consolation which occurs in the endurance of those sufferings which we also suffer: even our hope is firm for you. knowing that just as you are participants in the sufferings: so also in the consolation.

<margin>3</margin>
¶ For I do not want you to be unaware <note>original: "latere"—literally "to be hidden from you"</note> brothers, concerning our pressure / which was brought upon us in Asia: because we were excessively weighed down beyond our strength / so much so that we were weary of life. Nay rather, we had the pronouncement of death within ourselves: so that we should not trust in ourselves / but in God who raises the dead / who rescued and delivered us from such a death. In whom we have hoped: that he will yet deliver / as you also join in prayer for us, so that for the gift bestowed on me by many persons:

### ¶ VULGATE EDITION. ¶ THE SECOND EPISTLE OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE PAUL TO THE CORINTHIANS.

<margin>A</margin>
<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'P' similar to the first column but with a different arrangement of foliate ornamentation.</image-desc>
Paul, an apostle of CHRIST JESUS by the will of God, and Timothy the brother: to the church of God which is at Corinth with all the saints who are in all Achaia / grace to you and peace from God our father / and the Lord JESUS CHRIST.

<margin>B</margin>
Blessed be God & the father of our lord JESUS CHRIST, the father of mercies / and the God of all consolation, who consoles us in all our tribulation, so that we ourselves may be able to console those who are in any pressure: through the exhortation <note>original: "exhortationem"—the Vulgate uses this term where the Greek-based translation uses "consolationem." Both attempt to capture the Greek 'paraklesis,' which means to call someone to one’s side to comfort or encourage them</note> by which we ourselves are exhorted by God. Since just as the sufferings of CHRIST abound in us: so also through CHRIST our consolation abounds. But whether we are troubled for your exhortation & salvation / or we are consoled for your consolation / or we are exhorted for your exhortation and salvation which works the endurance of the same sufferings which we also suffer: so that our hope may be firm for you. knowing that just as you are companions of the sufferings: so you shall be also of the consolation.

<margin>C</margin>

**EPISTLE.**

<margin>A</margin>

And I hope that you will understand even until the end, just as you have understood us in part: that we are your glory, just as you also are ours in the day of our Lord JESUS CHRIST.

<margin>D</margin>
And in this confidence I wanted to come to you first, so that you might have a second grace <note>original: "gratiam"—here referring to the benefit or spiritual gift of a second apostolic visit</note>, and to pass through you into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come to you, and by you be set on my way into Judea. When I therefore intended this, did I use lightness? <note>original: "levitate"—meaning fickleness or being light-headed in making decisions</note> Or the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, so that with me there should be "Yes" and "No"? <note>Paul is defending himself against accusations that he is unreliable; he argues his "Yes" is not a "No."</note> But as God is faithful, our word which was among you was not "Yes" and "No," but in Him it was "Yes." For the Son of God, JESUS CHRIST, who was preached among you by us—by me and Silvanus <note>Also known as Silas</note> and Timothy—was not "Yes" and "No," but in Him was "Yes." For however many are the promises of God, in Him they are "Yes." And therefore through Him is the "Amen" to God for your glory. <margin>a</margin> Now He who confirms us with you in CHRIST, and who has anointed us, is God; who also has sealed us and given the pledge <note>original: "pignus"—a legal term for a down payment or security deposit ensuring a future transaction; here, the Holy Spirit is the "down payment" of heaven.</note> of the Spirit in our hearts. But I call God as a witness upon my soul, that to spare you I did not come again to Corinth. Not because we have dominion over your faith, but we are helpers of your joy. For by faith you stand.

<margin>II</margin> <margin>A</margin> But I determined this very thing with myself: that I would not come to you again in sorrow. For if I make you sad, then who is there to make me glad but the one who is made sad by me? For out of much tribulation <margin>B</margin> and anguish of heart I wrote to you with many tears, not so that you might be saddened, but that you might know...

<margin>10</margin> <insert>¶</insert> But if anyone has caused sorrow, he has not caused me sorrow except in part, so that I may not seem to burden you all. For we are not (as many are) hawking the word of God <note>original: "cauponantes"—a vivid term referring to hucksters or dishonest wine-merchants who water down their product for profit.</note>; but as if from sincerity, but as if from God, in the sight of God, we speak in CHRIST.

# Epistle
->A IV<-

<column-break/>

ministers of the new testament: not of the letter but of the spirit. For the letter kills: but the spirit gives life. But if the ministry of death, engraved in letters upon stones, was in glory, so that the children of Israel could not look intently at the face of Moses, because of the glory of his countenance which is passing away: how shall the <margin>C</margin> ministry of the spirit not be more in glory? For if the ministry of condemnation is in glory: much more does the ministry of justice <note>original: "iustitiae"—righteousness or divine justice</note> abound in glory. For even that which was made glorious had no glory in this respect, because of the surpassing glory. For if that which is passing away came through glory: much more that which remains is in glory. Having therefore such hope: we use great boldness. And not as Moses, who put a veil over his face, so that the children of Israel might not look intently at the face of that which is passing away: but their senses <margin>D</margin> were dulled. For until this very day: that same veil remains in the reading of the old testament, not being lifted (because in CHRIST it is made void), but even until this day when Moses is read, a veil is placed over their heart. But when he shall have turned to God: the veil shall be taken away. Now the Lord is the spirit. And where the spirit of the Lord is: there is liberty. But we all, beholding the glory of the Lord with an unveiled face: are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, as by the spirit of the Lord. Therefore, having this ministry: according as we have obtained mercy, we do not faint. But we renounce the hidden things of shame: not walking in craftiness, nor adulterating the word of God, but by the manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man's conscience before God. But if our gospel be also hidden: it is hidden in those who are perishing. In whom the god of this world <note>original: "deus huius saeculi"—referring to the devil or the spiritual blindness of the age</note> has blinded the minds of unbelievers: so that the light of the gospel of the glory of CHRIST, who is the image of God, should not shine. For we do not preach ourselves: but JESUS CHRIST our Lord.

d.ij.

<margin>19</margin> ...but ourselves as your servants for the sake of JESUS. For it is God who commanded light to shine out of darkness, and he himself has shone in our hearts for the illumination of the knowledge of the glory of God in the person of JESUS CHRIST. But we have this treasure in earthenware vessels <note>original: "testaceis vasis" — pots made of baked clay, emphasizing human fragility and the common nature of the messengers</note> (so that the surpassing excellence of the power may be of God, and not from us). We are pressed in every way, but not suffocated; in need, but not destitute; suffering persecution, but not forsaken; cast down, but not perishing; always carrying the dying <note>original: "mortificationem" — refers to the "deadness" or the state of being put to death, mimicking Christ's sufferings</note> of the Lord JESUS in our body, so that the life of JESUS may also be manifested in our body. For while we live, we are continually being handed over to death for the sake of JESUS, so that the life of JESUS may be manifested in our mortal flesh. Therefore, death works in us, but <margin>20</margin> life works in you. Since we have the same spirit of faith, according to what is written: "I believed, and therefore I have spoken," we also believe, and therefore we speak. We know that he who raised the Lord JESUS will also raise us through JESUS and will place us with you. For all things are for your sake, so that grace, having been multiplied through many, may overflow in thanksgiving to the glory of God. For this reason, we do not give up. For even though our outer man is decaying, our inner man is renewed from day to day. For our light burden of pressure <note>original: "pressurae" — refers to the trials and afflictions of the ministry</note>, which is temporary, produces for us an eternal weight of glory beyond all excellence, while we look not at the things that are seen, but at the things that are not seen. For the things that are seen <margin>21</margin> are temporary, but the things that are not seen are eternal. For we have found it to be certain that if our earthly house of this dwelling is dissolved, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens. For in this we groan, desiring to be clothed over with our dwelling which is from heaven—if indeed, being clothed, we are not found naked. For we who are in this dwelling groan, being burdened...

But we have this treasure in clay vessels <note>original: "vasis fictilibus"</note>, so that the loftiness of the power may be of God, and not from us. ...clothed: because we do not wish to be stripped, but rather to be **clothed over**, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life. <margin>B</margin> Now he who has prepared us for this very thing is God, who has given us the **pledge** <note>original: "pignus" — a token of security or a deposit</note> of the Spirit. Therefore, being always confident and knowing that while we are in this body, we are wandering away from the Lord. For we walk by **faith**, and not by **sight**. But we are confident and have a good will rather to wander away from the body and to be present with the Lord. And therefore we strive, whether absent or present, to please him. For we must all be made manifest before the **judgment seat** <note>original: "tribunal" — the raised platform where a Roman official sat to deliver a verdict, known in Greek as the Bema</note> of **CHRIST**, so that each one may receive back the proper things of the body according to what he has done, whether good or evil. We do not commend ourselves to you again, but we give you an opportunity to glory on our behalf, so that you may have something for those who glory in appearance and <margin>C</margin> not in heart. For if we are out of our mind, it is for God; if we are sober, it is for you. For the **charity** <note>original: "charitas" — the selfless, divine love of Christ</note> of **CHRIST** constrains us, judging this: that if one died for all, then all have died. our [authority]: I shall not be ashamed. ### III 2 Corinthians

I drained other churches, taking pay <note>original: "stipendium" — referring to wages or support provided to a soldier or worker</note> for your service. ### IV Galatians

[The one who worked] in Peter for the apostleship of the circumcision <note>the mission to the Jewish people</note>, worked also in me among the Gentiles. And when they had recognized the grace that was given to me, James and Cephas <note>the Aramaic name for Peter, meaning 'Rock'</note> and John, who seemed to be pillars, gave the right hands of fellowship to me and Barnabas. <margin>C</margin> They asked only that we should be mindful of the poor; which was the very thing I was eager to do. But when Cephas came to Antioch, I resisted him to his face, because he was to be blamed. For before certain men came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles. But when they arrived, he began to withdraw and separate himself, fearing those who were of the circumcision. And the other Jews consented to his pretense, so that even Barnabas was led away by them into that same pretense <note>original: "simulatione," referring to acting out of harmony with one’s true convictions; hypocrisy</note>. But when I saw that they were not walking uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of everyone: "If you, being a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?" We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners from the Gentiles,
<margin>D</margin> knowing that a person is not justified by the works of the law, except through faith in JESUS CHRIST: even we believe in CHRIST JESUS, so that we may be justified by the faith of CHRIST, and not by the works of the law. For this reason: by the works of the law, no flesh <note>meaning no human being</note> shall be justified. But if, while seeking to be justified in CHRIST, we ourselves are found to be sinners, is CHRIST then a minister of sin? Certainly not. For if I build up again those things which I destroyed, I prove myself a transgressor. For through the law, I died to the law, so that I might live for God. I have been fixed to the cross with CHRIST. Yet I live; or rather, not I, but CHRIST lives in me. And what I now live in the flesh, I live in the faith of the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself up for me. I do not cast away the grace of God. For if righteousness comes through the law, then CHRIST died for nothing.

<margin>A III</margin> O foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you that you should not obey the truth? Before whose very eyes JESUS CHRIST was publicly portrayed as crucified among you. This only I want to learn from you: did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? Are you so foolish that, though [you began with the Spirit...]

<meta>This page continues Paul’s passionate appeal to the Galatians. Having previously discussed the history of his ministry and his rebuke of Peter, he now turns to a sophisticated scriptural allegory involving Abraham’s family to illustrate the difference between being a "slave" to the Law and a "free child" of God’s promise.</meta>

# THE EPISTLE TO THE GALATIANS

...and would have given them to me. Have I therefore become your enemy by telling you the truth? These people pay court to you, but not for any good purpose; they want to exclude you from us so that you will pay court to them. It is always a good thing to be courted in a good cause, and not only when I am present with you. My little children, for whom I am in labor again <note>Paul uses the metaphor of childbirth to describe his agony and effort in helping the Galatians grow in their faith</note> until CHRIST is formed in you. I wish I could be with you right now and change my tone, because I am perplexed by you. Tell me, you who want to be under the law: have you not read the law? For it is written that Abraham had two sons: one by a bondwoman <note>Hagar</note> and one by a free woman <note>Sarah</note>. But the son of the bondwoman was born according to the flesh, while the son of the free woman was born through the promise.
<margin>D</margin> These things are spoken through an allegory. For these are the two covenants. One is from Mount Sinai, bearing children for slavery; this is Hagar. For Sinai is a mountain in Arabia that corresponds to the Jerusalem that now exists, for she is in slavery with her children. But the Jerusalem that is above is free, and she is our mother. For it is written: "Rejoice, you barren woman who does not bear; break forth and shout, you who are not in labor; for the children of the desolate woman are more numerous than those of her who has a husband." Now we, brothers, are children of the promise like Isaac. But just as then the one born according to the flesh persecuted the one born according to the spirit, so it is now. But what does the scripture say? "Cast out the bondwoman and her son. For the son of the bondwoman shall not be an heir with the son of the free woman." Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free woman;
<margin>A V</margin> and it is in this freedom that CHRIST has set us free.
Stand firm, then, and do not be held again by the yoke of slavery. Look, I, Paul, say to you: if you receive circumcision, CHRIST will be of no benefit to you. I testify again to every man who allows himself to be circumcised that he is a debtor to the entire law. You have been separated from CHRIST, you who seek to be justified in the law; you have fallen from grace. For we, through the spirit, by faith, wait for the hope of righteousness.
<margin>B</margin> For in CHRIST JESUS neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any power, but only faith that works through love <note>original: "charitatem," often translated as charity or divine love</note>.

<column-break/>

...would have given them to me. In what way have I become your enemy: by telling you the truth? They have a zeal for you, but not rightly; rather, they want to exclude you, so that you might have zeal for them. Zeal in a good thing is always good, and not only when I am present among you. My little children: for whom I am in labor again, until CHRIST is formed in you. I wish I were present with you now and could change my voice, rather than being so indignant with you. Tell me, you who want to be under the law: do you not hear the law? For it is written: that Abraham had two sons, one from a bondwoman and one from a free woman. But the one from the bondwoman was indeed born according to the flesh; however, the one from the free woman was through the promise. These things are spoken as an allegory. For these are two testaments. One from Mount Sinai, giving birth into slavery: which is Hagar. For this is Hagar (Sinai is a mountain in Arabia, and it borders upon the one that is now Jerusalem), for she serves with her children. But the other, the Jerusalem above, is free, and she is the mother of us all. For it is written: "Rejoice, barren woman who does not bear, break forth and cry out, you who do not labor: because the children of the deserted woman are many, more than of her who has a husband." Now we, brothers, are the children of Isaac according to the promise. But just as then he who was born according to the flesh persecuted him who was born according to the spirit: it is the same way now. But what does the scripture say? "Cast out the bondwoman and her son; for the son of the bondwoman shall not inherit with the son of the free woman." Therefore, brothers: we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free woman. Stand firm, therefore, in that liberty by which CHRIST has freed us, and do not be held back again by the yoke of slavery. And I, Paul, say to you: that if you are circumcised, CHRIST will benefit you nothing. I witness again to every circumcised man: that he is bound to fulfill the entire law. You are cut off from CHRIST, you who are justified in the law; you have fallen away from grace. For we in spirit: look for the hope of righteousness from faith. For in CHRIST JESUS: neither circumcision can do anything, nor uncircumcision, but faith which works through affection <note>original: "dilectionem," a term for high esteem or brotherly love</note>.

<summary>Paul uses the story of Abraham's two sons, Ishmael and Isaac, as an allegory to argue that the Galatians should live as "free" children of God's promise rather than "slaves" to the Old Testament Law. He warns that adopting Jewish circumcision would signify a return to legalism and a rejection of Christ's grace.</summary>

<margin>C</margin>
Some indeed preach CHRIST even because of envy and rivalry; but some also because of good will. Some preach out of charity, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the gospel. But others announce CHRIST out of contention, not sincerely: thinking that they stir up pressure for my chains <note>original: "vinculis meis"; Paul refers to his literal imprisonment, traditionally thought to be in Rome</note>. What then? So long as in every way, whether by pretense or in truth, CHRIST is announced: and in this I rejoice, and I will continue to rejoice. For I know that this will result in my salvation: through your prayer and the provision of the spirit of JESUS CHRIST, according to my expectation and hope, that in nothing shall I be put to shame: but with all confidence, as always, even now shall CHRIST be magnified in my body, whether by life or by death. For to me, to live is CHRIST: and to die is gain <note>original: "mori lucrum"; one of the most famous expressions of Paul's faith, viewing death as a reward because it brings union with Christ</note>. But if living here in the flesh is the fruit of my labor: then I do not know what I should choose.
<margin>D</margin>
I am hard-pressed between the two: having a desire to be dissolved and to be with CHRIST, which is much, much better; yet to remain in the flesh is necessary for your sake. And having this confidence, I know that I shall remain and continue with all of you for your progress and the joy of your faith: so that your rejoicing may abound in CHRIST JESUS in me, through my coming to you again. Only conduct yourselves in a manner worthy of the gospel of CHRIST: so that whether I come and see you, or being absent I hear of you, that you stand in one spirit, with one mind working together for the faith of the gospel. and be in no way terrified by your adversaries, which is to them a cause of perdition, but to you a cause of salvation. And this is from God, because it is granted to you for the sake of CHRIST: not only that you should believe in him, but also that you should suffer for his sake, having the same struggle which you saw in me: and now have heard of me.

# EPISTLE.

<margin>D</margin>

However, I thought it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother and co-worker and fellow-soldier, but your apostle <note>original: "apostolum"; here used in the sense of a messenger or envoy sent by a church</note> and the minister to my needs. Since indeed he was longing for you all: and was heavy-hearted because you had heard he had been sick. For indeed he was sick even unto death: but God had mercy on him. And not only on him, but also on me, lest I should have sorrow upon sorrow. Therefore I sent him more hurriedly: so that when you see him again you may rejoice, and I may be without sorrow. Because for the work of CHRIST he came close to death, handing over his life <note>original: "tradens animam suam"</note>, so that he might fulfill what was lacking from you toward my service.

<margin>A III</margin>
### For the rest, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. 
To write the same things to you is not tedious to me, but for you it is necessary. Watch out for the dogs. Watch out for the evil workers. Watch out for the "mutilation" <note>original: "concisionem"; a mocking play on the word "circumcision," suggesting that ritual cutting without faith is merely a physical wounding</note>. For we are the circumcision, we who serve God in spirit: and glory in CHRIST JESUS, and have no confidence in the flesh, though I too might have confidence in the flesh.

<margin>C</margin>
If anyone else seems to trust in the flesh: I more so—circumcised on the eighth day, of the race of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews, according to the law a Pharisee, according to zeal persecuting the church of God, according to the righteousness which is in the law, living without blame. But what things were gain to me, these I have counted as loss for the sake of CHRIST. Yet indeed I also count all things to be loss because of the surpassing knowledge of JESUS CHRIST my Lord: for whom I have suffered the loss of all things. And I count them as dung, that I may gain CHRIST: and be found in him, not having my own righteousness which is from the law, but that which is from the faith of JESUS CHRIST, which is the righteousness from God.

immediately: as soon as I see how my affairs will be. But I trust in the Lord that I also will come quickly.

Watch out for the dogs, watch out for the evil workers, watch out for the "cutting" <note>original: "concisionem"</note>. But what things seemed gain to me: these I have counted loss for CHRIST. And I consider them to be dunghills <note>original: "sterquilinia"</note>: so that I may gain CHRIST, and be found in him, not having my own righteousness which is of the law, but that righteousness which is from God through the faith of CHRIST.

### EPISTLE TO THE PHILIPPIANS

<margin>D</margin> [I hope to send] them: as soon as I see how things go with me. But I trust in the Lord that I myself will also come soon. However, I thought it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother, co-worker, and fellow soldier, but your apostle <note>original: "apostolum"; in this context, it refers to a messenger or envoy sent by the church at Philippi to Paul.</note> and the minister to my needs. Since indeed he was longing for you all and was distressed because you had heard he was sick. For indeed he was sick to the point of death, but God had mercy on him. And not only on him, but also on me, so that I would not have sorrow upon sorrow. Therefore I sent him more eagerly, so that seeing him again you might rejoice, and I might be without sorrow. Receive him therefore with all joy in the Lord and hold such people in honor. Because for the work of CHRIST he came close to death, handing over his life to fulfill what was lacking from you toward my service.

<margin>A III</margin> **For the rest, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord.** Writing the same things to you is not tedious for me, and for you it is necessary. Watch out for the dogs. Watch out for the evil workers. Watch out for the mutilation <note>original: "concisionem"; a derogatory play on the word for circumcision, implying a mere cutting of the flesh rather than a spiritual covenant.</note>. For we are the circumcision, who serve God in spirit and glory in CHRIST JESUS, and do not have confidence in the flesh—though I also might have confidence in the flesh. <margin>C</margin> If anyone else thinks he can trust in the flesh, I more so: circumcised on the eighth day, of the race of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; according to the law, a Pharisee; according to zeal, persecuting the church of God; according to the righteousness which is in the law, living without blame. But those things which were gains to me, these I have considered as loss for the sake of CHRIST. Furthermore, I also consider all things to be loss because of the surpassing knowledge of JESUS CHRIST my Lord, for whose sake I have made all things a loss. And I count them as dung <note>original: "stercora"; a very strong term for waste or refuse, emphasizing how little he values his former status.</note>, so that I may gain CHRIST and be found in him, not having my own righteousness which is from the law, but that which is through the faith of CHRIST JESUS, which is righteousness from God.

<column-break/>

...immediately: as soon as I see what will happen concerning me. But I trust in the Lord that I too will come quickly.

<margin>8</margin> ¶ Moreover, I thought it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother and co-worker and fellow soldier, but your messenger and minister to my lack: since certainly he was affected by a longing for all of you. And he was troubled for this very reason, that you had heard he had suffered from ill health. For indeed he labored close to death. But God had mercy on him: and not only on him but also on me, so that I would not endure sorrow upon sorrow. Therefore I sent him more diligently: so that seeing him you might rejoice again, and I might be less sad. Receive him therefore in the Lord with all joy: and hold those who are like this as honorable. For on account of the work of CHRIST he approached even unto death. From his own deliberation he was about to lay down his life: to supply what was lacking from you in my service.

<margin>9</margin> As for what remains, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. Writing these things to you is not troublesome for me, while for you it is safe. Beware the dogs, beware the evil workers, beware the mutilation. For we are the circumcision: who through the spirit maintain the worship of God and glory in CHRIST JESUS, and by no means have confidence in the flesh. # EPISTLE.

...[which] surpasses all understanding: let it guard your hearts and your minds in CHRIST JESUS. Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever things are modest, whatever things are just, whatever things are holy, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good report: if there be any virtue, if there be any praise of discipline, think on these things. What you have both learned and received, and heard and seen in me: do these things, and the God of peace will be with you. But I rejoiced in the Lord greatly: that at last you have flourished again <note>original: "refloruiśtis"; Paul uses a botanical metaphor, suggesting the Philippians' care for him has "bloomed" again like a plant in spring.</note> in your care for me, just as you also felt. But you were busy. <margin>C</margin> Not as though I speak because of lack. For I have learned to be content in whatever state I am. I know how to be humbled, and I know how to abound. Everywhere and in all things I am instructed: both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer lack. I can do all things in him who strengthens me. Nevertheless, you have done well in sharing in my tribulation. And you Philippians know also: that in the beginning of the Gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving, except you alone. For even to Thessalonica you sent once and twice for my use. Not because I seek a gift, but I seek fruit <margin>D</margin> abounding to your account. But I have everything and abound. I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus <note>A messenger sent by the Philippian church to bring aid to Paul while he was imprisoned.</note> the things which you sent, a sweet-smelling fragrance, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God. And may my God fulfill every desire of yours, according to his riches in glory in CHRIST JESUS. Now to God and our Father be glory forever and ever. Amen. Greet every saint in CHRIST JESUS. The brothers who are with me greet you. All the saints greet you, especially those who are of Caesar's household <note>original: "de Cæsaris domo"; this refers to the imperial civil service or slaves and freedmen working in the Emperor's administration in Rome.</note>. The grace of our Lord JESUS CHRIST be with your spirit. Amen.

...of understanding <note>original: "dinis", the suffix of "certitudinis" or "plenitudinis," referring to the full assurance of understanding</note> in the knowledge of the mystery of God, both of the Father and of **CHRIST**: in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. <margin>6</margin> ¶Now this I say, so that no one may deceive you <note>original: "paralogizet," a Greek-derived term for using false logic or deceptive arguments</note> with persuasive speech. For even if I am absent in body, yet I am with you in spirit: rejoicing and observing your order, and the steadfastness of your faith which is in **CHRIST**. Therefore, as you have received **JESUS CHRIST** the Lord: walk in him, rooted and built up in him, and established in the faith, just as you have been taught, abounding in it with thanksgiving. Beware lest anyone plunder you through philosophy and empty deceit according to the tradition of men, according to the elements of the world: and not <margin>7</margin> according to **CHRIST**. ¶Because in him dwells all the fullness of the divinity bodily, and you are filled in him: who is the head of all principality and power. In whom also you were circumcised with a circumcision not made by hands, in the stripping away of the body of the sins of the flesh, in the circumcision of **CHRIST**, buried with him in baptism. In whom also you have risen again through faith, by the operation of God who raised him from the dead. And when you were dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh: he has brought you to life together with him, pardoning all your sins, blotting out the handwriting <note>original: "chirographum," a legal document of debt or a bond signed by a debtor</note> of decrees that was against us, which was contrary to us. And he took it out of the way, fastening it to the cross; stripping the principalities and powers, he led them away boldly, <margin>8</margin> triumphing over them in himself. ¶Therefore, let no one judge you in food or in drink, or in respect of a feast day or a new moon, or of the sabbaths: which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of <margin>9</margin> **CHRIST**. ¶Let no one cheat you of your prize by a self-willed humility and the religion of angels, entering into things which he has not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind, and not holding fast to the Head, from whom the whole body, supplied and joined together through joints and ligaments, grows with an <margin>10</margin> increase from God. ¶If you are dead with **CHRIST** from the elements of the world: why, as if living in the world, do you seek after doctrines: "Do not touch, do not taste, do not handle..."

<column-break/>

...of understanding in the recognition of the mystery of God the Father and of **JESUS CHRIST**: in whom <margin>A</margin> are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. This I say, so that no one may deceive you with lofty words. For even if I am absent in body, yet I am with you in spirit, rejoicing and seeing your order and the firmament of that faith of yours which is in **CHRIST**. Therefore, as you have received <margin>B</margin> **JESUS CHRIST** our Lord, walk in him: rooted and built upon him, and confirmed in the faith just as you learned, abounding in it with thanksgiving. See that no one deceives you through philosophy and empty delusion: according to the tradition of men, according to the elements of the world, and not according to **CHRIST**. Because in him dwells all the fullness of the divinity bodily: and you are filled in him, who is the head of all principality and power. In whom also you were circumcised with a circumcision not made by hands, in the stripping away of the body of the flesh: but in the circumcision of **CHRIST**, buried with him in baptism, in which also you rose again through the faith of the operation of God: who raised him from the dead. <margin>C</margin> And you, when you were dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, he has brought to life with him: granting you all your sins, blotting out the handwriting of the decree that was against us, which was contrary to us. And he took it from our midst, fastening it to the cross: and stripping the principalities and powers, he led them away confidently, openly triumphing over them in himself. Therefore, let no one judge you <margin>D</margin> in food or in drink, or in respect of a feast day, or of the new moon or of the sabbaths: which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of **CHRIST**. Let no one seduce you at his will: walking in humility and the religion of angels in things he has not seen, puffed up in vain by the sense of his flesh, and not holding to the Head, from whom the whole body, supplied and constructed through connections and joints, grows into an increase from God. # UNDERSTANDING FROM THE GREEK. FIRST EPISTLE OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE PAUL TO THE THESSALONIANS.

<image-desc>A small decorative woodcut initial 'P' depicting a landscape or architectural scene inside the letter frame.</image-desc>
<margin>1</margin> Paul and Silvanus and Timothy: to the church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord **JESUS CHRIST**. Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord **JESUS CHRIST**.

<margin>2</margin> We give thanks to God always for all of you, making mention of you in our prayers, steadily mindful of the work of your faith, and the labor of your love, and the waiting of your hope in our Lord **JESUS CHRIST**, before God and our Father.

<margin>3</margin> Knowing, beloved brothers, your election by God: because our gospel was not among you in word only, but also in power, and in the Holy Spirit, and in much fullness of certainty, just as you know what kind of men we were among you for your sake. And you were imitators of me, that is, of the Lord: receiving the word in much pressure <note>original: "pressura." This suggests a crushing weight of affliction.</note>, with the joy of the Holy Spirit, so that you were an example to all believers in Macedonia and Achaia. For from you the word of the Lord was spread abroad, not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but also in every place your faith which is toward God has been carried, so that there is no necessity for us to speak anything. For they themselves announce concerning us what kind of entrance we had to you: and in what way you were converted to God from idols, to serve the living and true God, and to wait for his son from heaven (whom he raised from the dead), **JESUS**, who rescues us from the wrath that is coming.

<margin>4</margin> For you yourselves know, brothers, our entrance which was among you: that it was not in vain. But having suffered before...

Epaphras greets you, who is one of you, a servant of **CHRIST JESUS**, always anxious for you in prayers: that you may stand perfect and full in the whole will of God. For I bear testimony for him: that he has much labor for you, and for those who are at Laodicea, and those who are at Hierapolis. Luke the most dear physician greets you, and Demas. Greet the brothers who are at Laodicea: and Nymphas, and the church which is in his house. And when this epistle has been read among you: see to it that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans. And that which is from the Laodiceans: let it be read by you. And say to Archippus: See the ministry which you have received in the Lord: that you fulfill it. The greeting: by my hand, Paul's. Be mindful of my chains. The grace of our Lord **JESUS CHRIST** be with you. Amen.

Epaphras greets you, who is one of yours, a servant of **CHRIST**, always striving for you in prayers: that you may persist as consummate and replenished in every matter by the will of God. For I bear testimony for him: that he has much zeal <note>original: "Zelum." This version emphasizes Epaphras's internal passion rather than just his external "labor."</note> for you, and for those who are at Laodicea, and those who are at Hierapolis. Luke the beloved physician greets you, and Demas. Greet the brothers who are at Laodicea: and Nymphas, and his household church. And when the epistle has been read among you: see to it that it is read in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you read the one that is from the Laodiceans <note>Scholars have long debated whether this refers to a lost letter Paul wrote to Laodicea or perhaps the Epistle to the Ephesians.</note>. And say to Archippus: see the administration <note>original: "adminiſtrationem." A more technical term for a specific duty or office.</note> which you have received in the Lord, that you might fulfill it. The greeting, by my hand, Paul's. Remember my bonds, grace be with you. Amen.

...suffered much and were treated shamefully, as you know, in Philippi: we had confidence in our God to speak to you the gospel of God in much concern <note>original: "sollicitudine." so that that day does not catch you like a thief. For you are all children of light and children of the day. We are not of the night, nor of darkness. Therefore let us not sleep as the others do; but let us watch and be <term>temperate<gloss>sober-minded and self-controlled</gloss></term>. For those who sleep, sleep at night; and those who are drunk, are drunk at night. But we who are of the day, let us be temperate, clothed in the breastplate of faith and love, and a helmet which is the hope of salvation. <margin>A</margin> so that that day may not catch you like a thief. For you are all children of the light and children of the day. We are not of the night nor of darkness. ...from which arises envy, contention, blasphemies, evil suspicions, and the conflicts of men corrupt in mind and destitute of the truth, thinking that godliness is a gain. ¶ Stay far away from such as these. To be sure, godliness with contentment is a huge gain. For we brought nothing into this world: and it is manifest that we can take nothing out. Pursue justice, godliness, faith, love, patience, and gentleness. Fight the good fight of faith. Lay hold of eternal life: to which you were also called, and have confessed a good confession in the sight of many witnesses. ¶ I charge you before God, who gives life to all things, and **CHRIST JESUS** who witnessed under Pontius Pilate a good confession: that you keep the precept unstained and without reproach, until the appearance of our Lord **JESUS CHRIST**. To whom be honor and eternal power. Amen. ¶ Charge those who are rich in the present world: that they do not think loftily, nor hope in the uncertainty of riches, but in the living God (who offers us all things opulently for delightful use) that they do well, that they be rich in good works, that they contribute easily, being ready to share, treasuring up for themselves a good foundation for the future: so that they may lay hold of life (which is truly so). ¶ O Timothy, guard the deposit, turning away from profane vanities of words and the oppositions of <term>gnosis<gloss>original: "gnoseos"; the Greek word for "knowledge," used here to describe false intellectual or spiritual claims</gloss></term>, falsely so called. Which some, promising: have wandered from the faith. Grace be with you. Amen.

Paul, an apostle of **JESUS CHRIST** by the will of God, according to the promise of life which is in **CHRIST JESUS**: To Timothy, my beloved son, grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father, and **CHRIST JESUS** our Lord. <margin>2</margin> ¶ I give thanks to God, whom I worship from my ancestors <note>original: "a progenitoribus"; Paul emphasizes his continuity with his Jewish heritage</note> with a pure conscience: because I have a constant memory of you in my prayers, night and day, desiring to see you, being mindful of your tears, so that I may be filled with joy: when I call to mind the unfeigned love which is in you, and the faith which first dwelt in your grandmother Lois, and in your mother Eunice, and I am also persuaded <margin>3</margin> that it is in you as well. ¶ For which cause I admonish you: that you stir up the gift of God which is in you through faith and the laying on of my hands. For God has not given us the spirit of timidity: but of power, of love, and of purity <note>original: "castimoniæ"; the Vulgate uses "sobrietatis" (sobriety/self-control)</note>. Therefore, do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but labor together for the gospel, according to the power of God who has saved us, and called us with a holy calling. Not according to our works: but according to his own purpose and grace which was given to us in **CHRIST JESUS** before the ages of time <note>original: "ante tempora saecularia"; referring to eternity before the creation of the world</note>, but is now made manifest by the appearing of our Savior **JESUS CHRIST**. Who has indeed abolished death, and has brought life and incorruptibility to light through the gospel: in which I am appointed a herald and an apostle and a teacher of the Gentiles. For which cause

Just as Jannes and Mambres <note>original: "Mambres"; names traditionally assigned to the Egyptian sorcerers who opposed Moses in Exodus</note> resisted Moses: so these men also resist the truth / men corrupted in mind / reprobate concerning the faith / but they shall proceed no further. For I am already being poured out as a sacrifice <note>original: "delibor"; a metaphor of a drink offering poured on an altar</note>: and the time of my departure is at hand. I have fought the good fight / I have finished the course / I have kept the faith. As for the rest, there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness / which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall render to me on that day. And not only to me: but also to those who love his coming.
