# Bishop Linus

...to reign forever and to dissolve all the kingdoms of the world. And Patroclus said: "Indeed, Caesar; he shall destroy all kingdoms that are under heaven, and everything under heaven shall serve him, because he alone is the King of kings and Lord of lords." But Nero gave him a slap <note>original: "alapa" — a blow with the open hand, often used as a gesture of contempt or a legal act in freeing a slave</note>, saying: "So, you serve as a soldier for that king?" And Patroclus, exulting, said: "Yes, for he raised me from the dead."

Then Barnabas, and Justus, and a certain Paul <note>This refers to a different individual named Paul who was a member of the imperial staff, not the Apostle himself</note>, and Arion the Cappadocian, and Festus the Galatian—who were ministers of Caesar and stood by him constantly—said to Nero: "Why, Caesar, do you strike a young man who answers so rightly, so prudently, and so truthfully? For we, too, serve as soldiers for that unconquered King, JESUS CHRIST our Lord."

But when Nero heard them say with one mind and in the same words that Jesus was an unconquered king, he shut them in prison so that he might greatly torture those whom he had previously loved so much. He ordered a search for the servants of that King and issued an edict: that wherever they were found, all of CHRIST’s soldiers should be punished through various torments without interrogation. 

Whence, by much searching by the ministers of the state and the promoters of the "storehouses of malice" <note>original: "apothecæ malignitatis" — a metaphorical description of the Emperor's agents or perhaps a specific administrative office</note>, many servants of God were sought out and found; they were led into the presence of Caesar. Among them was PAUL, wearing his customary chains for the name of CHRIST, led as a prisoner. All the other prisoners looked at him so intently that Nero was easily able to recognize, without anyone pointing him out, that this was the very PAUL who presided over the soldiers of the Great King.

Understanding that he was the leader and the teacher of Christ’s servants, Nero said to him: "O man, servant of I-know-not-which king, but my prisoner: what possessed you to enter the Roman Empire in secret and to withdraw men from my service, collecting them for your own leadership?" 

PAUL, filled with the Holy Spirit, said steadfastly in the ears of all who were present: "Nero, we do not only collect soldiers from your corner, but from the whole world. For this command was given to me: that I should reject no one from any nation who wishes to serve my eternal King. For the Lord is powerful, dispensing the richest gifts to all with a generous hand according to each person's merit. If it should seem good to you also to believe in Him and obey Him faithfully, you will not repent of it. Moreover, do not think that the riches of this world, or splendor, or glory, should save you; but if you are subject to Him, you will be safe forever. For when He comes to judge the living and the dead, He will dissolve the form of this world through fire. And the gifts prepared before the foundation of the world and hidden for ages, which will never fail and which will exclude all want, He will bestow upon His soldiers."

Hearing this, Nero was inflamed with rage because the apostle had said the form of the world would be dissolved by fire. He ordered all of Christ’s soldiers to be burned with fire. However, by a decree of the Senate <note>original: "senatusconsulto"</note>, he ordered PAUL to be beheaded according to Roman laws, as one guilty of treason <term>maiestas: the crime of "diminished majesty" or treason against the Emperor and the state</term>. 

He handed him over to the prefects Longinus and Megistus, and to the centurion Acestus, so that they might lead him outside the city and, providing a spectacle of his killing to the people, order him to be beheaded. To them, PAUL preached the word of salvation without ceasing. 

Nero, driven by the working of the devil, sent ministers and officers with speed throughout the entire city and the surrounding region to search with the greatest diligence for those hiding and to kill all Christians who were revealed. Because of this, such a vast multitude of Christians was killed that the Roman people rushed into the palace by force and, attempting to stir up a sedition against Caesar, shouted: "Put a limit, Caesar, to this most unjust command! Restrain your irrational fury! Let your cruelty suffice, for you are overstepping the bounds of belief. These are our own people whom you are destroying. They protect the Roman Empire. You are taking away Roman strength, Caesar, which stood terrible to all nations because of the great number of these soldiers." 

Then Nero, terrified by the outcry of the people, put forward another edict: that no one should dare to touch the Christians or bring any trouble upon them until a report of the fullest investigation was referred to Caesar from the information of any accuser. Because of this, PAUL was brought before him once again. 

When Nero saw him, he cried out most vehemently, saying: "Take away the sorcerer, behead the imposter! Do not allow this weaver of charms <note>original: "carminatorem" — likely implying a user of magic incantations or songs</note> to live! Destroy the one who alienates the senses, take away from the face of the earth the changer of minds!" 

To him, PAUL said: "Nero, for a short time I shall suffer, but I shall live forever with my God and eternal King, JESUS CHRIST, who is coming to judge the world in a blaze of fire."

Nero then said to Megistus, Longinus, and Acestus: "Take his head away quickly, and let him flatter himself about eternal life, and let him realize that I am the unconquered king, who has bound him and overcome him by killing him." 

But PAUL said: "So that you may know, Nero, that after my beheading I live eternally for my unconquered King, and that you are the one defeated—you who think you conquer—when my head has been cut off, I will appear to you alive. And you will be able to know that death and life serve my Lord JESUS CHRIST, to whom belongs every kingdom, and to whom He wills He shall give it. All victory is His; and whom He wishes to conquer, He makes to triumph magnificently. And He alone is unconquered: the King forever." 

And with these things said, PAUL was led to his punishment. As he was being led, Longinus, Megistus, and Acestus said to him: "Tell us, PAUL: where is that King, and where did He appear to you, and how did you know Him, and what good did He grant you, or what will He grant you, that..."

<header>II</header>

<meta>Handwritten note in red ink in top right margin: "Passion of Paul,"</meta>

"...is this how most ardently you Christians love him? That by no means do you wish to lend your assent to our religion so that you might live and enjoy the good things of this life; but instead, you consider it more pleasant than any delight to die for him through various torments? For this seems a great error: to hate this pleasant life and to embrace punishments and death with all your desire." But **PAVLVS** replied:

<margin>Passion of Paul</margin>
"O wise men, flourishing with good sense: leave behind the darkness of ignorance and error, by whose mist the nobility of your intelligence is clouded over, so that you cannot see the truth that lies hidden within you. Turn the eyes of your mind toward the eternal and true light, so that you may first be able to know yourselves, and thus arrive with joy at the knowledge of that King, and remain safe and unharmed from the fire that is about to come upon the whole world. For we do not serve as soldiers for any earthly king, as you think, but for the living God, the King of the heavens and of all ages. Because of the iniquities committed in this world, He will come as a judge and will judge the world through fire. Blessed, however, will be the man who believes in Him. For he shall have eternal life and shall live for all ages of ages. But most unhappy is he—none more unhappy than he—who, despising the riches of His goodness and patience, does not turn to Him; for he shall perish forever. For this reason, He who made heaven and earth descended from heaven to earth, and He who made man was made man: so that man, turning from his iniquity and leaving behind the vain things and mute idols <note>original: "simulacra muta" — lifeless statues or images worshipped as gods</note> which he most wickedly worships instead of God, might serve Him who made him, and adore Him before whom the angels tremble and all the powers of heaven worship. When this is done, He makes that person a true worshiper and His servant, a companion and associate of His angels—namely, the holy and blessed spirits. And not without merit: because God is spirit. And He will make a companion for the holy spirits of the one who worships and adores Him in spirit and truth. But the one who refuses to believe in Him, He will return as a companion and accomplice to the wicked demons; He will send that fugitive into the torment of eternal burning, to the scorching and perpetual fire. This is the fire to come, through which God is to judge the world. Therefore, O wise men, let your prudence judge for itself who made the world, since it did not come forth without a maker. Consider who made man, for as the divine oracles testify, he did not make himself. Take heed: for vain idols are not gods, but the handiwork of men, and demons lie hidden within those very works. Though they may seem to agree in this—that they unanimously desire the destruction of the human race—they nonetheless undoubtedly distrust one another in various ways. 'For there is no peace for the wicked,' says the Lord. For there is a reason why they hasten to destroy men and have them as companions in their punishments: they know that men will ascend through God's grace into the heavenly dwelling from which those spirits themselves fell through their own pride. O men of civil wit, recognize this: the name of divinity is by no means divided among many. For there is one God, from whom are all things; and one Lord JESUS CHRIST, through whom are all things; and one Holy Spirit, in whom all things consist. All things faithfully obey Him, and there is no division in the divinity, for it lacks plurality. Take heed, citizens of Rome: consider where discord was born, and by what reasoning it increased and grew so far and wide so miserably, and why such a multitude of not deities, but miserable monsters of gods, have emerged. Namely, because many began to want to be princes and tyrants, and masters not of the conquered, but of men who shared their own nature. From this, submerged in a storm of ignorance and cast down into the abyss of their own arrogance, each one either borrowed or established a god for his own power. For miserable men reached such madness that they established most wretched men as gods for themselves, whom they wished to please so that they might escape a terrible death. But since some of them did not see fit to acknowledge God, they were given over to their own lusts, to perform those works which the Roman laws punish with execration. And what was said in the most holy words was fulfilled in them: 'Let those who make them become like them' <note>A reference to Psalm 115:8, suggesting that those who make idols become as lifeless and spiritually blind as the objects they craft</note>. For they made miserable gods for themselves, and they themselves became miserable. And they have fallen into such insanity that they say to a wooden trunk, 'You are our god,' and to a stone, 'Help us,' and they adore a crafted log while they are warmed by its woodchips. At this, many crowds of listeners, raising their voices with lamentation, said: 'We have erred, we have sinned, we have acted unjustly. O teacher of salvation and shower of eternal life and truth: be merciful to us, that we may be rescued from the snares of sin, and be able to escape the fire by which the world will be burned, and in which every unhappy and wicked soul will be tortured.'" 

Then **PAVLVS** said: "O brother men, whose hearts the Lord has touched with His spirit: stand faithfully in the faith. For ministers of eternal salvation will be present by whom you shall be baptized; and by persevering well in the charity of our Lord JESUS CHRIST, you shall be saved forever." 

Longinus, Megistus, and Acestus <note>Traditionally identified as the Roman soldiers or prefects tasked with guarding Paul</note>, speaking to the apostle more privately, said: "We ask you, lord, make us be enrolled in the service [militia] of the eternal King, so that we may be able to escape the coming fire and become participants in the perpetual kingdom; and then we will let you go. Or rather, wherever you decide to go, we will be your companions on the journey and obedient even unto death." To them, **PAVLVS** said: "My brothers, I am not a fugitive, but a legitimate soldier of my King. For if I knew that I would die, and not..."

<meta>This page continues the narrative of the Apostle Paul’s final hours in Rome under the reign of Nero. Having previously refused to escape, Paul now prepares for his execution, interacting with both faithful followers and skeptical Roman soldiers.</meta>

### THE WRITINGS OF BISHOP LINUS <note>Linus was traditionally the successor to St. Peter as Bishop of Rome; this text is part of a famous apocryphal account of Paul's death attributed to him.</note>

...rather I might reach life and glory through this death: I would not only do what you ask, but I would even demand this of you. Now, however, I have not run in vain through many tribulations, nor do I desire to suffer without cause. For the crown of victory remains for me, which he in whom I have believed will give to me, and of which I am certain. For I go to him, and with him I shall come when he comes in his glory, and that of the Father and the holy angels, to judge the world. Therefore, I despise this death, and I will not listen to your petition to flee, nor will I do it.

Those people, however, weeping, said to him: "What then are we to do? How shall we live once you have been punished? And how shall we be able to reach that one in whom you persuade us to believe?" And while they were saying these things among themselves, and a great crowd was raising their voices aloud, Nero sent certain soldiers, Parthenius and Pheretas, to see if **PAUL** had already been killed. When they arrived, they found him still living and speaking to the people at great length. **PAUL**, calling them to himself, said to them: "Men and brothers, believe in the living God, who will raise me and all who believe in him from the dead." But they, answering, said: "We will go first to Caesar to report everything. And when that for which we were sent has been completed—and when you are dead and have risen again as you say—then we will believe in your king. But now, end these delays by which you defer the command, and go to the destined place where you may receive the sentence deservedly dictated." **PAUL** also said to them: "You have more need of my staying in the flesh if you wish to believe than I, who go to life through death. But let us go now, exulting in the name of our Lord **JESUS CHRIST**."

And as they were going to the place of the passion, accompanied by innumerable crowds of people, he came to the gate of the city of Rome where he met a most noble matron named Plautilla, a most fervent lover of the apostles and a worshiper of the divine religion. Weeping, she began to commend herself to his prayers. To her, **PAUL** said: "Go, Plautilla, daughter of eternal salvation; lend me the cloth with which you cover your head <note>The Latin 'maphorte' refers to a short veil or hood.</note>, and move aside a little way because of the press of the crowd. Wait for me here until I return to you and restore the favor to you. For I shall bind my eyes with it in place of a burial cloth; and as a pledge of my love for you for the sake of **CHRIST’S** name, I shall leave it to you as I go to him." She quickly handed over the cloth and obeyed just as the apostle had commanded her. 

But both Parthenius and Pheretas mocked her, saying: "Why do you believe this impostor and magician? Why do you lose a perfectly good cloth? You will gain nothing from him in this world." But **PAUL** said to her: "Truly, daughter, wait for my arrival, and I shall bring the signs of my death to you in the small cloth, for I am about to live with **CHRIST**." Meanwhile, Longinus, Magistus, and Acestus <note>Tradition identifies these as the soldiers who were converted by Paul's execution.</note>, while they were insisting more earnestly for their own salvation, inquiring how they might reach the true life, heard from the blessed apostle: "Brothers and my sons: as soon as I have been beheaded, you and the other ministers of my execution should withdraw from the place where the Lord deigns to call me; faithful men will seize and bury my body. You, however, mark the place of my grave, and come there very early tomorrow at dawn. There you will find two men praying, **Titus** and **Luke**. Tell them the reason why I sent you, and they will give you the signs of salvation in the Lord. Do not, therefore, doubt to carry out what has been commanded of you. For as soon as you, believing, have been dipped in the sacred font and sanctified by the life-giving power of the divine mysteries, you will be cleansed without delay from all the contagions of sin—even from this crime committed against me, which you dread—and you will be made whiter than snow, enrolled in the ranks of **CHRIST’S** soldiers, and made co-heirs of the heavenly kingdom."

And having said these things, he arrived at the place of the passion. There, turning toward the east, with his hands stretched out toward heaven, he prayed for a long time with tears in Hebrew <note>original: "hebraice"</note> and gave thanks to God. And when he had finished his prayer in his native tongue, bidding farewell to the brothers, he blessed them. And binding his eyes with Plautilla’s veil, he fixed both knees on the ground and stretched out his neck. The executioner, raising his arms high, struck with all his might and cut off his head. 

After it was severed from the body, the name of our Lord **JESUS CHRIST** resounded in Hebrew <note>original: "hebraice"</note> in a clear voice. And immediately from his body a wave of milk leapt out onto the soldier's garments, and afterward blood flowed out. As for the band with which he had bound his eyes, when certain people wanted to snatch it, it was not to be found. Such a sweetness of fragrance also wafted there, and such an immensity of light flashed from heaven at the moment of that beheading, that the eyes of mortals could not bear that splendor, nor could a human tongue describe the scent. Seeing the grace of God in the blessed apostle, all who were present were greatly amazed, praising and confessing for a long time the Lord **JESUS CHRIST**, the eternal and invincible King, whom the magnificent teacher and master of the nations, **PAUL**, had preached. 

Those who had been ordered to hasten his execution, returning, arrived at the city gate. There they found Plautilla, praising and glorifying the Lord in all that she had heard and seen through his holy apostle. And they asked her with mockery why she did not cover her head with the veil which she had lent... <note>The text ends mid-sentence.</note>

<meta>This page concludes the apocryphal "Passion of Paul," detailing the miraculous events following the Apostle's execution. It connects the previous page's discussion of Paul's impending death to the immediate aftermath, where he appears to both his followers and his executioner, Nero.</meta>

# THE PASSION OF PAUL

What happened to **PAUL**? She <note>Plautilla, a Roman matron who, according to legend, gave Paul her veil to bind his eyes at his execution.</note> replied, set ablaze with the heat of faith and with great courage: "O vain and wretched men, who know not how to believe what you see with your eyes and touch with your hands. For I truly hold the same cloth <note>original: "pannum"</note> which I had offered to him, precious from the flow of his blood. For coming from heaven, accompanied by a vast crowd of white-robed followers, he returned it to me in all truth. And returning favor for the kindness shown to him, he said: 'You, Plautilla, showed me service on earth; I shall most dutifully attend to you as you first depart for the kingdoms of heaven. For shortly he shall return for you, and I will show you the glory of the invincible King.'" And drawing the cloth from her bosom, soaked in rose-red blood, Plautilla showed it to them. Seized by extreme fear, they went with a quickened pace to Caesar, reporting what they had seen and heard.

But when he had heard this, he was greatly amazed; and struck with massive astonishment, he began to consult with philosophers, friends, and ministers of the state, as well as those he could summon from the Senate, regarding the things reported to him. He held these conversations with fear, trembling, and a confusion of the senses. While they were wondering at these things and questioning one another, **PAUL** came at about the ninth hour <note>3:00 PM, a significant hour in Christian liturgy</note> while the doors were closed. He stood before Caesar and said: "O Caesar Nero, behold I, **PAUL**, a soldier of the eternal and invincible King; even now, you wretch, believe that I am not dead, but live for my God. For you, however, in not much time, unspeakable evils and the greatest punishment are imminent, and eternal destruction awaits you, because among your other worst crimes, you have unjustly shed much blood of the righteous." And saying this, he suddenly vanished. 

Nero, having heard these things and becoming as if insane, did not know what he should do. At the persuasion of his friends, he ordered Patroclus, Barnabas, and those who were bound with them to be released and allowed to go free wherever they wished. Finally, Longinus, Megistus, and Acestus <note>Legendary names for the soldiers who guarded or executed Paul and were converted by him.</note>—just as the Apostle had instructed them—came to his tomb early in the morning. There they saw two men praying, and **PAUL** standing in their midst. Being terrified by this wonderful vision, they shuddered and were afraid to approach closer. 

But Titus and Luke, returning to themselves from the ecstasy of prayer and seeing the prefects and the Centurion (who had been the ministers of **PAUL's** death) hurrying toward them, were seized by human terror and turned to flight. Then **PAUL** vanished from their eyes. The soldiers, however, cried out after them, saying: "We have not come to persecute you to death, as you suspect, O blessed men of God, but so that by believing, you might transfer us to eternal life through the water of baptism—just as the true teacher **PAUL** promised us, whom we saw standing and praying in your midst just a moment ago." 

Hearing this from them, Titus and Luke stood still with much gladness and spiritual joy, soon laying hands upon them and giving them the seal of eternal sanctification <note>A reference to the rite of baptism or confirmation.</note>. And so, with a fast continuing until evening, they were baptized in the name of our Lord **JESUS CHRIST**. To whom, with the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, is honor, glory, power, and dominion forever and ever. Amen.
